# Soft Polyurethane Foam Molded Article

## Overview

The present invention relates to a soft polyurethane foam molded article that features a mounting surface and is produced by foam-molding a foaming stock solution. This manufacturing approach enables the creation of a structured foam product with distinctive internal characteristics that vary systematically throughout the material.

## Layered Structure

The molded article is composed of multiple layered parts that are arranged in successive layers along the vertical direction—that is, the direction perpendicular to the mounting surface. This stratified configuration establishes the fundamental architecture of the foam article, with each layer contributing to the overall properties of the finished product.

## Cell Orientation Within Layers

A key feature of the invention lies in the geometry of the foaming cells contained within each layered part. Within any given layer, the individual cells exhibit a specific relationship between their lateral dimension and their vertical dimension. This relationship is expressed as a ratio of lateral size to vertical size, which progressively increases as the cells are located closer to the mounting surface. In other words, cells positioned nearer the mounting surface become comparatively wider and flatter, while those situated farther away retain a more vertically elongated shape.

## Cell Ratio Behavior at Layer Boundaries

An additional and important characteristic emerges at the boundaries where two vertically adjacent layered parts meet. At each such boundary, the cell ratio in the layer positioned nearer the mounting surface is lower than the cell ratio in the layer positioned nearer the opposite back surface. This creates a distinct transition in cell geometry across the interface between adjacent layers, producing a repeating pattern of variation throughout the thickness of the molded article.

## Summary

Taken together, these features define a soft polyurethane foam molded article in which the internal cell structure is deliberately organized both within individual layers and across the boundaries between them. This carefully controlled variation in cell shape—characterized by the increasing lateral-to-vertical ratio toward the mounting surface within each layer, combined with the discontinuity in cell ratio at the layer boundaries—distinguishes the invention and contributes to its intended performance characteristics.

# Soft Polyurethane Foam Molded Article with Layered Cell Structure

## Field and Background

The present invention relates to the structure of soft polyurethane foam molded articles, which are widely used in applications such as cushioning materials, seating components, and various padding elements where both comfort and durability are essential. In these applications, the mechanical behavior of the foam—including its resilience, load-bearing capacity, and feel under compression—depends heavily on the internal architecture of the foaming cells that make up the material.

Conventional foam molded products often exhibit relatively uniform cell structures throughout their thickness, which can limit the ability to tailor mechanical performance to the specific demands placed on different surfaces of the article. In particular, the surface that is mounted against a supporting frame or base (the mounting surface) and the surface that faces outward or is exposed (the back surface) frequently experience different types and magnitudes of mechanical loading. A single uniform structure cannot optimally serve both.

## Summary of the Invention

To address these structural considerations, the present invention provides a foam-molded product constructed with multiple parts that are layered in the vertical direction—that is, stacked through the thickness of the article between the mounting surface and the back surface. The defining feature of this construction lies in the controlled orientation and proportioning of the foaming cells within and across these layers.

Within the article, each foaming cell can be characterized by the ratio of its lateral (horizontal) dimension to its vertical dimension. According to the invention, this lateral-to-vertical size ratio increases progressively as one moves closer to the mounting surface. In other words, cells located nearer the mounting surface are comparatively flattened or elongated in the horizontal direction, whereas cells located farther from the mounting surface exhibit proportionally greater vertical extension.

A further characteristic feature concerns the behavior of this ratio at the boundaries between adjacent layers. At each layer boundary, the lateral-to-vertical size ratio is lower on the mounting-surface side of the boundary than on the back-surface side. This creates a distinct, stepped variation in cell geometry across the interfaces between the vertically stacked layers, rather than a purely continuous gradient.

## Advantages

This layered cell-orientation design enables a controlled and deliberate variation in the foam structure across the thickness of the article. By governing how the cell aspect ratio changes both within each layer and across the layer boundaries, the manufacturer can precisely engineer how the foam responds to compression and other mechanical stresses at different depths.

As a result, the invention offers improved mechanical properties that can be specifically tailored relative to both the mounting surface and the back surface. The regions near the mounting surface, with their higher lateral-to-vertical cell ratios, and the regions near the back surface, with their differing cell proportions, can each be optimized to provide the appropriate support, cushioning, and durability characteristics demanded by their respective functions. This affords a foam molded article whose overall performance is superior to that achievable with a conventional, uniformly structured foam.

# Patent Abstract

## Soft Polyurethane Foam Molded Article with Layered Structures and Varying Foaming Cell Ratios

**ABSTRACT**

A soft polyurethane foam molded article comprising a plurality of integrally formed layered structures arranged in a stacked configuration relative to a mounting surface. The molded article is characterized by a graduated cellular structure in which the foaming cell ratio varies progressively across the layered structures as a function of distance from the mounting surface. In one embodiment, the article comprises a base layer disposed adjacent to the mounting surface having a first foaming cell ratio, and one or more overlying layers each having a foaming cell ratio different from the base layer, thereby establishing a density gradient throughout the molded article. The layer proximate to the mounting surface exhibits a relatively lower foaming cell ratio to provide enhanced structural rigidity and support, while layers distal to the mounting surface exhibit a relatively higher foaming cell ratio to provide increased cushioning, softness, and compressibility. The varying foaming cell ratios are achieved through controlled foaming conditions during a molding process, wherein the cell size, cell density, and cell wall thickness are selectively regulated within each respective layer. The resulting molded article provides improved load-bearing characteristics, tailored comfort properties, and durable adhesion to the mounting surface, rendering the article suitable for use in cushioning applications, seating, vehicle interior components, and comparable applications requiring differentiated mechanical properties across a unitary foam body.
